description: Neon is a chemical element with symbol Ne and atomic number 10, the second noble gas in the periodic table. It is a colorless, odorless, inert monatomic gas under standard conditions with approximately two-thirds the density of air. Neon was discovered in 1898 by British chemists William Ramsay and Morris Travers.
uses: Neon is used in low-voltage neon glow lamps, high-voltage discharge tubes, and neon advertising signs where it emits a distinct reddish-orange glow. The same red emission line is responsible for the characteristic red light of helium-neon lasers. Although neon has some applications in plasma tubes and as a refrigerant, its commercial uses are relatively limited.
characteristics: Neon is the second-lightest noble gas and is colorless and odorless. It glows reddish-orange in a vacuum discharge tube and has over 40 times the refrigerating capacity per unit volume of liquid helium and three times that of liquid hydrogen. Despite helium surpassing neon in ionization energy, neon is theorized to be the chemically least reactive of all elements, with no stable neutral or covalent neon compounds known to exist under any pressure or temperature.
